years_since_diagnosis.evidence: Diagnosed at 19. Seven years of hell.

severity.evidence: Passing blood, severe pain, living in bathroom; required step-up through mesalamine, prednisone, methotrexate, Humira, and now Stelara; multiple flares causing school interruptions.

disease_control.evidence: Now on Stelara. Helps both conditions somewhat. Neither perfect but both manageable.

treatments.reason_stopped: not explicitly stated; escalated to other therapies
triggered hypomanic episode; not stated as sole reason for stopping
treatments.evidence: Started with mesalamine and prednisone. Prednisone triggered my first hypomanic episode.

treatments.reason_stopped: severe nausea; eventually escalated to biologic
treatments.evidence: Started methotrexate. Helped Crohn's but made me so nauseous.

treatments.reason_stopped: developed severe Humira-induced eczema; switched to Stelara
treatments.evidence: Started Humira at 21. Game changer initially. Could eat, energy returned, finished school. But developed severe eczema. Dermatologist said might be Humira-induced.
Now on Stelara. Helps both conditions somewhat. Neither perfect but both manageable.

encounters.evidence: Finally went to health center. They actually took it seriously. Referred immediately.
Colonoscopy at 19 was terrifying. Doctor said Crohn's. Started with mesalamine and prednisone... Started methotrexate... Started Humira at 21... Now on Stelara.

referral_steps_gp_to_prescriber.evidence: Health center referred directly to GI specialist who managed all IBD treatment including biologics.

extraction_notes: Lamotrigine (mood stabilizer), vitamin D, B12, iron, probiotic, and topical steroids for eczema excluded from IBD treatment list as they treat comorbidities (bipolar II, eczema) or are supplements. Humira-induced eczema noted as adverse effect leading to switch to Stelara. Bipolar II diagnosis came at age 25 (last year). Surgery discussed as a future possibility if Stelara fails but not yet planned. Ketamine therapy mentioned as a personal interest for depression, not an IBD treatment.
